title: CIRE: LLVM Analysis for Floating-Point Rounding Error Affected by Precision and Optimizations
problem: Mixed-precision optimization requires understanding floating-point rounding error across compiler optimizations
motivation: Programmers need tools to explore mixed-precision settings while maintaining accuracy and improving performance
method: CIRE analyzes floating-point rounding error—the inaccuracies that accumulate when calculations are rounded to fit limited precision—by reading LLVM code (the compiler's intermediate representation) without running it. It breaks the code into basic blocks (straight-line sections between branches) and calculates accumulated rounding error through up to 10^5 floating-point operations per block. The analysis tracks how compiler optimizations interact with precision settings to change where and how rounding errors occur.
key_novelty: CIRE statically measures floating-point rounding error in LLVM code while accounting for how both compiler optimizations and precision settings affect the error.
contributions: CiRE static analysis tool for rounding error
Analysis of up to 10^5 operators per basic block
